headline: MIT engineers used AI to design mRNA vaccine particles that stayed fully active for over two months without freezing, in tests on cells and animals.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a practical result with a published study, but it is preclinical and has not been tried in people.
summary: Drug Discovery News reports that MIT engineers, in a Nature Biotechnology study, used an AI-guided search to dry and stabilise the fat-based particles that carry mRNA in COVID-19 vaccines of the Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech type, which kept full activity at 37 degrees Celsius for over two months. Mice given particles stored that way responded as well as to fresh vaccine, and the formulation also worked in dissolvable microneedle skin patches in rodents and non-human primates, but no human trials are reported.
importance_line: Vaccine programmes in places without reliable freezers could benefit if this holds up, but the evidence so far comes from cells and animals, not people.
